revisit: NISAR passed over our sites every 12 days in June–October 2026 (one pass missing on 2 Aug), day or night, through clouds.

headline_numbers.label: Rogun reservoir
headline_numbers.detail: 13.9 → 20.0 km² of water, 27 Jun → 13 Oct 2026; level ≈ 1,115 → 1,128 m (radar + terrain estimate, ±10 m)

headline_numbers.label: Nurek reservoir
headline_numbers.detail: 74.3 → 89.7 km², seasonal refill, same orbit as Rogun

headline_numbers.label: Rogun dam
headline_numbers.detail: no measurable motion beyond about ±3 cm (InSAR, 8 pairs, ionosphere removed)

headline_numbers.label: Vakhsh cotton fields
headline_numbers.detail: 696 km² of farmland grew denser June → September (HV radar signal)

headline_numbers.label: Nepal flood path
headline_numbers.detail: km² of river channel changed along the Trishuli, Betrawati → Galchhi

audiences.insight: Both reservoirs on the Vakhsh can be measured every 12 days from space, in any weather. In summer 2026 Rogun gained a third of its area, with the biggest jump between mid-August and early September; Nurek refilled by about a fifth.
audiences.action: Track filling against the operating plan without waiting for clear skies; compare area and estimated level with gauge readings.

audiences.insight: The Rogun dam showed no measurable movement (within ±3 cm). One small slope (0.36 km²) above the reservoir moved steadily, about 12 cm along the radar line of sight in 3.5 months.
audiences.action: Put that slope on the field-inspection list. In Nepal, the radar shows exactly which stretch of the river and which villages the flood reached, days later, through monsoon clouds.

audiences.insight: The radar follows crop growth in the Vakhsh valley through the season and flags fields that changed early.
audiences.action: Use the 12-day signal to see where crops are growing or already cleared, field by field, without cloud gaps.

audiences.insight: One river, two stories: people building a new reservoir (Rogun) and a natural disaster reshaping a valley (Nepal), both seen by the same satellite.
audiences.action: Use the before/after slider and the timeline as a ready classroom example of how humans and nature change the land.

audiences.insight: Changes upstream — a filling reservoir, a moving slope, a flood path — show up on the map weeks before they are obvious on the ground.
audiences.action: Check your area on the map; the data is open and updated every 12 days.

natural_vs_human.human: Rogun and Nurek: dams filling a mountain valley (Tajikistan)
natural_vs_human.natural: Bhote Koshi–Trishuli flood of 26 Aug 2026, triggered by an ice and rock avalanche (Nepal)
natural_vs_human.rhythm: Seasonal: Nurek refills every summer and is drawn down in winter; crops grow and are harvested; monsoon floods

caveats: Level, InSAR and harvest results are estimates from provisional NISAR data; see each manifest for method and uncertainty.
